title: Lesson 1 Quiz: Income, Spending, and Budgeting
description: A short quiz to check what you learned in this lesson. Submitting it completes the lesson's quiz requirement, and your score is recorded separately.

history.note: AI-written question draft. Not reviewed or approved by a human (admin); do not give to students.

Comprehensive audit: l1-q2 choices made parallel and neutral (fixed prices stated once in the stem); l1-q3 choices made parallel so the key is not the only hedged or differently built choice; l1-q5 stem fixes the saving goal so only one choice balances the budget, and difficulty set to intermediate. Not reviewed or approved by a human.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Maya's weekly pay stub shows gross pay of $640. Deductions are $88 for taxes and $32 for a retirement plan contribution. What is her net (take-home) pay for the week, in dollars? (Enter a number only.)
Which of these is the best example of a variable expense for a student? Assume each plan, pass, or subscription has a set price.

Hypothetical example: Two students each pay $60 a month for a car insurance policy. Student A drives to a night job with no bus service. Student B lives next to a train station and drives mainly on weekends for fun. Which classification of the insurance fits best?

choices.text: A fixed need for A and a variable want for B
A variable need for A and a fixed want for B
A fixed want for A and a fixed need for B
A fixed need for A and a fixed want for B

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Leo wants $1,100 for a used scooter in 6 months. He has already saved $260. Ignoring interest, how much must he save each month to reach the goal on time, in dollars? (Enter a number only.)

Hypothetical example: Rosa's net income is $1,800 a month, and her gross pay is $2,150. Her plan adds up to $1,950: $200 of saving for emergencies, $1,550 of fixed expenses and needs, and $200 of variable wants such as eating out. She wants to keep saving $200 a month. Which response balances her budget (spending + saving = net income) while keeping her saving goal?

choices.text: Cut her variable wants by $150 a month
Plan from her $2,150 gross pay instead
Put the $150 gap on a credit card each month
Stop saving until her spending fits her pay
